title: Cross-team objective lifecycle and initiative sync runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational runbook that folds company-level OKRs into a predictable initiative cadence for cross-functional teams. The runbook should define roles, meeting rhythm, artifact templates (roadmap slices, dependency register, escalation ladder), and automation touchpoints (notifying owners, syncing into Linear and the roadmap spreadsheet). Goal is to reduce OKR drift during planning cycles and make cross-team handoffs explicit.
background: Over the last 2 quarters we observed repeated drift between company-level objectives and team-level delivery: missed alignment checkpoints, unclear dependencies, and inconsistent escalation paths. This causes reactive re-prioritization during sprints and increases the chance of initiatives missing objective signals. Execs requested a lightweight operational layer that scales across 8+ product and infra teams.
goals: Define a 6-week cadence that aligns with company cycles and enables two planning touchpoints per quarter
Deliver templates and checklists for PMs and Eng leads to register initiative intents against OKRs
Provide a dependency register format that integrates with Linear and supports automated notifications
Create an escalation rubric and decision matrix for cross-team conflicts
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc is published in Confluence and linked from the company OKR hub
Three pilot teams complete a full cadence (intent -> intake -> kickoff -> check-in) using the runbook templates
Automated Linear labels and Slack notifications are configured for the dependency register integration
A post-pilot readout includes measurable improvement in alignment (qualitative feedback + one metric)
